top.line: A reply to the FCA's plan for agentic finance, with a payments agent's policy filled in.
top.para: The FCA will develop a trusted framework for agentic finance with agent identity, delegated authority, accountability and execution. Most of that is open work we have already published. This maps the speech to it and fills in all four elements for an invented bank's payments agent. It is CC BY: adopt it, or write your own as a graph and connect them.

in-short.line: Seven points: the framework, our open work, and a worked example.
in-short.para: The FCA's four elements match what we publish: delegated authority as grant, mandate and delta; accountability as a holder per rule; execution as who keeps each rule; identity, proposed here. A payments agent's policy shows all four, with three gaps and their holders.

speech.line: What Jessica Rusu said, from the FCA's drafted text.
speech.para: Adoption is here: 86% of firms use AI. Governance must come before deployment, senior managers are accountable, near misses must be reported, and agents need continuous, conditional assurance. The FCA will develop a framework for agentic finance with industry, regulators and frontier labs, and ended with an invitation to build it together.

four.line: Each of the four elements, against work already published here.
four.para: Delegated authority is the gap between can and may, which an Agent Behaviour Policy records. Execution is the level at which each rule is kept. Accountability is a holder per rule with a chain to the board, from risk acceptance. Identity is implicit in the ABP and explicit in the attestation layer.

example.line: An invented bank's payments agent, with all four elements filled in.
example.para: Twelve rows: grant, mandate, barrier, who keeps each rule and who holds it. Eight are kept by systems the agent cannot reach. Three are gaps: a setting the agent can flip, a rule only in the prompt, and an advice check that can miss. Each gap gets a holder's decision, and the policy is shown as JSON.

graphs.line: Adopt the open work, or write your own as a graph and connect them.
graphs.para: The ABP and these articles are CC BY. The FCA already publishes machine-readable rules through its Handbook API. If a regulator's expectations and a firm's policies are both graphs, edges connect them without a shared schema. The FCA's own agents could carry published behaviour policies too.

limits.line: No endorsement, a drafted speech, and an invented example.
limits.para: The FCA has not endorsed this; the alignment is my reading. The speech page is the drafted version. The bank, agent and rows are invented. Identity, holders, kept by and decision are proposed fields, and the framework itself does not exist yet.

sources.line: The speech, the ABP, and our earlier articles.
sources.para: The FCA speech of 19 October 2026, read that day; abp.sgit.ai version 0.12.1; and the articles on agent reach, enforcement levels, policy as code, a policy beside the prompt, liability, risk acceptance, the Thistlewood twin and the graph companies.
